thread:
ashley: Heads-up — scheduling a short "forced displacement" smoke check tomorrow 13:00 PT. Focus: mixed-capacity pools (reserved + spot), eviction handling, routing fallbacks, and cost telemetry. Keep it small (10% traffic) and quick. Reply if you can join or have concerns.

jordan: Can do. What's the success criteria?

ashley: Short list: 
- failover latency for in-flight requests < 30s to fallback model/region
- end-user error rate <= 2% during test window
- no regression in p95/p99 token latency beyond 20% for affected requests
- batch queue depth shouldn't exceed safe threshold (configured at 200)
- telemetry shows expected spike in reserved-usage and spot-fallback billing lines, cost delta < +10% for the hour :chart_with_upwards_trend:

devon: Quick runbook draft: 
1) divert 10% of production traffic to test route (traffic-mgr Canary rule)
2) trigger planned preempt on three spot nodes in pool-a (us-west-2 mixed pool)
3) observe routing -> reserved pool and cross-region fallback to us-west-1 if capacity short
4) run smoke evals against canary route (simple prompts)
5) revert routing after 10m and collect metrics/logs

mike: Add step 2a: kubectl simulate drain on targeted nodes for the runtime pods: 
```
kubectl cordon node-spot-03
kubectl drain node-spot-03 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
```
This mirrors provider interruption and forces graceful cache eviction.

sinead: Also ensure prefix KV cache warmup after we failover — otherwise we'll see large latency spike from cold KV fetches. Suggest we pre-populate cache in reserved pool with top-100 prompt prefixes.

ashley: Good call. I'll add a cache-warmup job to the runbook: `script/warm_kv.sh --prefix-list top100 --target reserved` before the drill.

ops-bot: Scheduled maintenance window recorded: id=fd-smoke-2028-07-07-1300, notify=on, autopause=false.

jordan: Who's owning the rollback if something goes sideways?

ashley: I'll own rollback with devon on standby. Rollback steps: remove canary routing, scale reserved pool to pre-test counts, and run `kubectl uncordon` on nodes.

devon: Telemetry to collect: route-level 1s/5s token histograms, node-level preemption events, batching queue length, cost lines (spot/reserved breakdown), and the live sample of 50 requests for manual inspection. Also capture JVM/GPU memory events for the serving processes.

mike: One more: we should test mixed-instance-type eviction — pick one A100 spot and one T4 spot so kernel paths change. Might reveal kernel selection bugs.

ashley: Agree. Test targets: node-spot-a100-07 and node-spot-t4-12. We'll mark them in the runbook.

sinead: Perf target: p99 <= 350ms for non-long-context requests. If we hit > 600ms at p99, we abort and rollback.

jordan: Cost acceptance: if reserved fallback increases bill by >12% in the hour, abort. We set alert on billing pipeline.

ashley: Ops checklist condensed for the thread: 
- [ ] 10% traffic canary configured (traffic-mgr)
- [ ] cache-warmup job queued
- [ ] owners: ashley (lead), devon (telemetry), jordan (routing), mike (node ops), sinead (perf)
- [ ] targeted nodes labeled and cordon/drain script ready
- [ ] rollback playbook validated
- [ ] post-mortem doc template pre-created

mike: I'll be online during test window and will run the drain commands.

devon: I'll wire up the metrics dashboard and set temporary alerts for the thresholds.

ashley: If no objections, we'll run it tomorrow. Please react with :thumbsup: if you're available or call out conflicts.

jordan: :thumbsup:

mike: :thumbsup:

devon: :thumbsup: I'll also capture heap dumps from the serving process if we see memory churn.

sinead: :thumbsup: I'll prepare the warm_kv payload and a short eval script.

ashley: Great — final note: keep messages short during the run. Use the incident channel if rollback needed. I'll paste the final runbook here 10m before start.

ops-bot: Reminder scheduled 10m before window.

ashley: (after-test) Quick post-run summary: routed 10% for 12m, drained two spot nodes, fallback to reserved + cross-region spill to us-west-1. Observations: p99 increased 18% (within target), error rate peaked at 1.4%, failover median 12s, 95th 28s, cost uplift ~7% for the test hour. We saw a transient KV cold-start spike for ~90s after failover. No crashes.

jordan: Nice run. Can we add a tiny pre-warm threshold so warm_kv runs closer to switch time to avoid the 90s cold spike?

sinead: I'll change warm_kv to run in two phases: bulk pre-populate at T-10m and quick delta at T-30s.

ashley: Postmortem and perf dashboards linked in the doc I just uploaded. Thanks all.

mike: Good exercise. Suggest we schedule a monthly mini-smoke for mixed pools.

ashley: Agreed. Adding to cadence. :white_check_mark:
